pairs.old: Operates the eCQM (electronic clinical quality measure) program, the Hospital Compare reporting system, and ties measures to payment in VBC programs.
pairs.new: Operates the eCQM (electronic clinical quality measure) program and the Care Compare public reporting site (which replaced Hospital Compare in 2020), and ties measures to payment in VBC programs.
pairs.claim: fallback: CMS operates 'the Hospital Compare reporting system' (retired 2020)
pairs.src: CMS consolidated Hospital Compare and its other Compare tools into Care Compare in 2020

pairs.old: National Quality Forum. Endorses measures through a consensus process — NQF endorsement is required for many federal quality programs.
pairs.new: National Quality Forum. Ran the consensus-based endorsement process federal programs relied on for two decades; since 2023 CMS's consensus-based entity contract has been held by Battelle (Partnership for Quality Measurement).
pairs.claim: fallback: NQF endorses measures and 'NQF endorsement is required for many federal quality programs' (stale since 2023)
pairs.src: CMS CBE contract awarded to Battelle 2023; endorsement via Partnership for Quality Measurement (matches lesson body hedis-p9)

pairs.old: Physicians now spend an estimated 15+ hours per week on documentation and reporting requirements. Studies show that every patient visit generates 2+ hours of EHR time.
pairs.new: Physicians report spending about 15.5 hours a week on paperwork and administration (Medscape, 2023). A 2016 time-and-motion study (Sinsky et al., Annals of Internal Medicine) found that for every hour of direct clinical face time, physicians spent nearly two more hours on EHR and desk work.
pairs.claim: fallback callout: '15+ hours per week'; 'every patient visit generates 2+ hours of EHR time'
pairs.src: Medscape Physician Compensation Report 2023 (15.5 h/week paperwork & administration); Sinsky et al., Ann Intern Med 2016, doi 10.7326/M16-0961 (nearly 2 h EHR/desk work per 1 h face time)
